source_title: Practical Limit of Index Calculus Algorithms for ECDLP over Prime Fields

review_provenance.method: Direct inspection of the author-linked WCC 2017 primary PDF.
review_provenance.boundary: This is a separate 12-page extended abstract, not a substitute for the unread CANS 2018 paper. It studies practicality at m=2 on selected small primes and explicitly makes no asymptotic-complexity claim.

locator.value: Section 1 final paragraph; Section 2.3; Sections 3.1-3.4, equations (4)-(8), Tables 1-2; Section 5

claims.paraphrase: For m=2 and selected favorable primes with N=2^r dividing p-1 and N approximately p^(1/2), the paper compares the original, symmetric, hybrid, resultant or GCD, and exhaustive presentations. The exhaustive k=1 presentation has the lowest reported time in every row of Table 1, while Table 2 reports lower resultant or GCD times at 12.1, 14.1, and 16.0 bits; the Groebner-based variants exhibit severe memory growth.
claims.boundary: The source explicitly disclaims asymptotic analysis. Results on selected toy primes, random prime-order curves, and one Magma platform do not price S17 at m=16, establish cryptographic scaling, or attack secp256k1.

claims.paraphrase: The paper extends the algebraic approach when p+1 has a large smooth factor by taking N-th roots of unity in the quadratic extension and tracing them to the base field. Its low-degree presentation is specialized to p congruent to 3 modulo 4, m=2, and N=2^r approximately p^(1/2).
claims.boundary: This is an extension-field trace factor-base construction, not the PKC 2016 auxiliary elliptic curve and self-isogeny construction. The 5.6-10.1-bit results do not resolve the secp256k1 auxiliary-curve property or its typed cell.
